en: Hello, the month-end cost cut-off is {cutoff}. For {project} we accrue {amount} for {vendor}. Please book it and reverse it on {reverse_on}.
Hello, invoice {inv_no} from {vendor} for {amount} on {project} is approved for payment. The due date is {due}. Please schedule the payment.
Hello, invoice {inv_no} from {vendor} for {amount} is disputed. The match check shows: {match}. Please do not pay it until the vendor sends a correction.
Hello, we drew {amount} from the reserve of {project} on {date} for: {reason}. The reserve left is {left}. Approved by {approved_by}.
Sponsor: change request price and effect
Hello, change request {change_id} "{title}" on {project} costs {extra_cost}, adds {extra_days} days and would be sold for {price}. Please decide before it affects the plan.
Hello {sponsor}, the forecast cost of {project} is {eac} against a budget of {bac}. The project is {pct} complete and the cost index is {cpi}.
Hello {sponsor}, please approve transfer {tr_id} on {project}: {amount} from {from_cat} to {to_cat}. Reason: {reason}.
Hello {contact}, we sent invoice {invoice_no} for {amount} for the milestone {milestone} on {project}. It is due on {due}. Please tell us if anything is missing.
Hello {contact}, invoice {invoice_no} for {amount} was due on {due} and is {days_late} days late. Please confirm the payment date.
Hello {contact}, invoice {invoice_no} for {amount} is {days_late} days past its due date. Please pay it this week or tell us the reason so that we can solve it together.
Hello {contact}, we received your payment of {amount} for invoice {invoice_no} on {paid_on}. Thank you.
Client contact: change order to sign
Hello {contact}, change request {change_id} "{title}" is priced at {price} and adds {extra_days} days. Please review and sign the change order so that we can start.
Hello {contact}, statement for {name}: billed {billed}, paid {paid}, balance {owed}. Please tell us the date you expect to pay the balance.
Hello {person}, your expense claim {claim_id} for {amount} ({description}) on {project} is returned. Please add the receipt or the reason and send it again.
Hello, the forecast of {project} is {over_by} above its budget and the cost index is {cpi}. The manager is {manager}. Please look at the recovery plan this week.
Project: {col:projects.name} ({col:projects.project_id}). Client: {col:projects.client}. Project manager: {col:projects.manager}. Sponsor: {col:projects.sponsor}. Status: {col:projects.status}.

The project runs from {col:projects.start} to {col:projects.end}. The approved budget is {col:projects.budget}. Approved and implemented changes add {col:projects.changes}, so the budget now is {col:projects.current}.

To date {col:projects.spent} is spent, which is {col:projects.used} of the budget now, and {col:projects.left} is left. The forecast cost at completion is {col:projects.eac}. The cost check shows: {col:projects.state}.
The contract price now is {col:projects.price_now}. The client has been billed {col:projects.billed} and has paid {col:projects.paid}, so {col:projects.owed} is still owed.
The budget changes only through an approved change request, a budget transfer or a draw on the reserve. Each is recorded, approved and signed.
Budget against actual report of {set:firm}, dated {today}.
The budget now is {col:forecast.bac}. The actual cost to date is {col:forecast.ac}, which is {col:forecast.used_pct} of the budget.
The project is {col:forecast.pct} complete against {col:forecast.planned_pct} planned by now. The earned value is {col:forecast.ev} and the planned value is {col:forecast.pv}.
The cost variance is {col:forecast.cv} and the schedule variance is {col:forecast.sv}. A negative figure means over cost or behind schedule.
The reserve planned is {col:forecast.reserve}. Of this {col:forecast.drawn} was drawn and {col:forecast.reserve_left} is left.
Budget now {col:forecast.bac}. Percent complete {col:forecast.pct}. Percent planned by now {col:forecast.planned_pct}.
Earned value is {col:forecast.ev}, planned value is {col:forecast.pv} and actual cost is {col:forecast.ac}.

The cost performance index is {col:forecast.cpi}: a value below 1 means each unit of money spent has earned less than a unit of planned work. The schedule performance index is {col:forecast.spi}: a value below 1 means the work is behind the plan.
The forecast at completion is {col:forecast.eac}, a variance of {col:forecast.vac} against the budget. The cost forecast shows: {col:forecast.state}.
Forecast at completion statement of {set:firm}, dated {today}.

The budget now is {col:forecast.bac} and the actual cost is {col:forecast.ac}. The estimate to complete is {col:forecast.etc}, which includes {col:forecast.known} of known extra cost that is not yet booked.

The forecast cost at completion is {col:forecast.eac}. The variance against the budget is {col:forecast.vac}, which is {col:forecast.vac_pct} of the budget. The forecast is over the budget by {col:forecast.over_by}.
The price now is {col:forecast.price} and the margin at completion is {col:forecast.margin}. The cost forecast shows: {col:forecast.state}.
The forecast is reviewed every month. Any recovery action is agreed with the sponsor and written in the project record.
Order amount: {col:orders.amount}. Tax: {col:orders.tax}. Total with tax: {col:orders.total}. Expected on: {col:orders.expected}.
Please confirm the order and the delivery date. Every invoice must show this order number. We pay an invoice when it matches the order and the goods or service received.
Request {col:requests.req_id}: {col:requests.item}, for {col:requests.project}. Requested by {col:requests.requested_by}. Estimated amount {col:requests.amount}. Needed by {col:requests.needed_by}.
{col:requests.quotes} quotes were received and the lowest price is {col:requests.best_price}.

Each quote is scored out of 100 with these weights: price {set:w_price}, lead time {set:w_lead} and quality {set:w_quality}. The chosen vendor is {col:requests.chosen_vendor}, on order {col:requests.order}.
When the chosen vendor does not have the highest score, the reason is written here and signed by the approver.
The payment terms are {col:vendors.terms_days} days. So far {col:vendors.invoiced} is invoiced and {col:vendors.outstanding} is unpaid. Open orders total {col:vendors.open}.

Invoices are paid on average after {col:vendors.avg_days} days. There are {col:vendors.overdue} overdue invoices and {col:vendors.disputed} disputed invoices. The vendor check shows: {col:vendors.state}.
We pay when the invoice matches the order and the goods received. A disputed invoice waits until the vendor sends a correction or a credit note.
The change adds {col:changes.extra_days} working days and is priced at {col:changes.price}. The status is {col:changes.status}, decided on {col:changes.decided_on}.
Work on the change starts when both parties have signed this order. The price is added to the contract price and the days are added to the plan. Other terms stay as agreed.
An amount of {col:contingency.amount} is drawn from the project reserve and moved to the category {col:contingency.category}. Reason: {col:contingency.reason}.

The reserve planned is {col:contingency.reserve}. After this draw {col:contingency.drawn} is drawn to date, {col:contingency.left} is left and {col:contingency.share} of the reserve is used. The reserve check shows: {col:contingency.check}.
The reserve pays only for risks and events that were not in the plan. Each draw is approved before the money is used.
The contract price now is {col:projects.price_now}. We have billed {col:projects.billed} and you have paid {col:projects.paid}. The balance owed is {col:projects.owed}.
Our payment terms are {col:projects.terms_days} days from the invoice date. Please tell us the date on which you expect to pay the balance, and tell us at once if any invoice is not clear.

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: warning days, amber and red share over plan, budget alert, tax rate, approval limit, accepted gap on invoices and the quote weights.
Fill Projects with each project: client, contact, terms, manager, sponsor, dates, budget, contract price and percent done. Spent, billed, paid and the forecast fill in from the other sheets.
Split each budget on Budget by Category and Phase Budgets, and set the planned spend of every month on Spend Plan by Month.
Enter every cost on Cost Lines with project, category, vendor and amount. Month, group, age and approval warnings fill in by themselves.
Type the percent complete on Projects and any known extra cost on Forecast at Completion. Read earned value, CPI, SPI and the final cost there and on Earned Value by Month.
Record each purchase on Purchase Requests, Quotes, Purchase Orders and Receipts. Quotes are scored with your weights and orders show goods received and the value still open.
Enter vendor invoices on Vendor Invoices: the due date comes from the vendor terms and the match checks the invoice against the order and the receipt.
Log every change on Change Costs, every draw on Contingency Log and every move between categories on Budget Transfers. Budgets and forecasts update.
Bill clients on Client Billing from your payment milestones and change orders, and enter month-end work not yet invoiced on Accruals. Expense Claims holds what the team spends.
Use the 14 calculators for earned value, estimates at completion, burn rate, quotes, order totals, three-way match, early payment, change price, reserve, margin, milestone invoices and what-if.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send one of 30 ready texts with the details already filled in.
Read Budget and Cost Dashboard and Charts every week: budget used, forecast, indexes, reserve, open orders, overdue invoices and client payments.
Keep the risks, issues, changes and decisions of every project in one workbook
Control project risks, issues, changes, decisions and assumptions
Risk register with score and expected cost
probability and impact from 1 to 5 give the score, the level and the expected cost; a check shows risks with no owner, no action or an overdue review
Risk heat map with live counts
the 25 cells of probability times impact count your open risks and their expected cost by themselves, so the steering group sees where the danger sits
for every project the reserve left is set against the expected cost of its open risks, with a warning when the reserve is tight or exhausted
each open risk can carry an indicator and a threshold, and the sheet shows when a trigger is close or reached before the risk occurs
Issue log with age, target and escalation level
severity sets the target days; age, days overdue and the level the issue should be escalated to are worked out for every open issue
Issue ageing by project and band
open issues are counted by project and age band, with the high and critical ones shown, so old problems cannot hide
Escalations with outcome and days open
every escalation records the level, the person, the date and the outcome, and shows when an escalation itself has waited too long
scope, cost and days effects set the approval route under your limits, and a check flags decisions that wait longer than your target
each change is assessed by area with a cost and days estimate, and the sheet shows the cost assessed so far and the assessments still open
Change board decisions with speed check
approved, rejected and deferred decisions are logged with their conditions and the days from the request, with a late-decision flag
decisions keep their options, who decided and the decide-by date, and proposed decisions past their date are flagged as overdue
Contingency drawdowns tied to the risk
each draw on a project reserve points to the risk that occurred, and shows the reserve planned, drawn to date, left and a warning before it runs out

Projects: sponsor, status and contingency reserve
One row per project with its manager, sponsor, dates, budget and contingency reserve; reserve drawn, reserve left, open risks and open issues fill in from the other sheets.
Team: who owns the risks, issues and actions
One row per team member with role and phone; the open risks, open issues and open actions each person owns and the overdue actions fill in from the other sheets.
Risk register: score, expected cost and review state
One row per risk with probability, impact from 1 to 5 and the cost if it occurs; score, level, expected cost, open actions, trigger state and a check for a missing owner, action or review fill in.
Risk heat map: open risks by probability and impact
One row for each of the 25 cells of probability times impact; the score, the level, the number of open risks and their expected cost in that cell fill in from the Risk Register.
Risk and issue actions: who does what by when
One row per action on a risk or an issue; kind, project, open or done, overdue state, days overdue and the owner phone fill in by themselves.
Risk reviews: planned, held and what they changed
One row per risk review with the planned and the actual date; days late, whether it was on time, the month and the phone of the person leading it fill in by themselves.
Risk triggers: early-warning indicators and thresholds
One row per early-warning indicator of an open risk with its threshold and the latest value; the risk, project, owner, share of the threshold and a state fill in by themselves.
Issue log: severity, age, due date and escalation level
One row per issue with severity, owner and due date; open or closed, age, target days, days overdue, state, the escalation level and the contact phones fill in by themselves.
Escalations: what went up a level and what came of it
One row per escalation of a risk or an issue with the level, the person, the date and the outcome; kind, project, title, days open and a state fill in by themselves.
Change requests: effect on cost and days, and the decision
One row per change request with its effect on scope, cost and days; days waiting, days to decide, approval route, cost assessed so far, open assessments and a decision check fill in by themselves.
Change impact: effect by area with cost and days
One row per area assessed for a change request with the effect, the cost and the days; the change title, project, state and the phone of the person assessing fill in by themselves.
Change board decisions: approved, rejected or deferred
One row per decision of the change board with its conditions; the change title, project, cost and days, days from the request, speed and the sponsor phone fill in by themselves.
Decision log: what was decided, by whom, and what is waiting
One row per decision with the options considered and who decided; age, days late, a state for decisions waiting past their date, the project manager and the sponsor phone fill in by themselves.
Assumptions: what the plan relies on and whether it holds
One row per assumption with the owner, the date by which it must be validated and what happens if it is wrong; days to validate, a state, the client contact and the owner phone fill in by themselves.
Dependencies: what the plan needs from others
One row per dependency or constraint with who gives and who needs it, the date needed, and whether it is outside the firm; days left, a state and the phones fill in by themselves.
Lessons learned: what happened and what we change
One row per lesson with the phase, what happened, the lesson and the action to take; the year, a state for the action and the owner phone fill in by themselves.
Contingency drawdowns: reserve used by risks that occurred
One row per draw on a project reserve, linked to the risk that occurred; project, reserve planned, drawn to date, reserve left, share used and a check fill in by themselves.
RAID summary: one line per project
One row per project; type the focus of the week. Open risks, expected cost against the reserve, issues, changes, assumptions and dependencies count themselves from the other sheets.
Exposure by level: open risks and cost per project
One row for each project and risk level; the number of open risks, their expected cost and the share of the project exposure fill in from the Risk Register.
Issue ageing: open issues per project and age band
One row for each project and age band with the first and last day of the band; the number of open issues and of high or critical ones in the band fill in from the Issue Log.

Risk owner: your risk is due for review
Hello {owner}, risk {risk_id} "{title}" is due for review on {review}. Please check its score and its mitigation.

Hello {owner}, issue {issue_id} "{title}" is {over} days overdue. Please send me a new date today.

Risk register report of a project
Project: {col:raid.project}. Project manager: {col:raid.manager}. Sponsor: {col:raid.sponsor}. Status: {col:raid.pstatus}. Health: {col:raid.health}.
The register holds {col:raid.open_risks} open risks. Of these, {col:raid.high_risks} are high or critical and {col:raid.critical_risks} are critical. The open risk score is {col:raid.risk_score}.
{col:raid.no_owner} open risks have no owner and {col:raid.overdue_review} reviews are overdue.

The expected cost of the open risks is {col:raid.exposure}. The reserve planned is {col:raid.reserve}, of which {col:raid.drawn} is drawn and {col:raid.left} is left. The reserve check shows: {col:raid.reserve_check}.
Heat map summary for the steering group
Heat map summary for the steering group of {set:firm}, dated {today}.

Of {col:raid.open_risks} open risks, {col:raid.critical_risks} are in the critical zone of the heat map and {col:raid.high_risks} are high or critical. Together the open risks carry a score of {col:raid.risk_score}.
Their expected cost is {col:raid.exposure}. The reserve left is {col:raid.left}, so the exposure above the reserve is {col:raid.short}. The reserve check shows: {col:raid.reserve_check}.
We ask the group to decide how the open exposure is covered and to confirm the owners of the highest risks.
The log holds {col:raid.open_issues} open issues. {col:raid.critical_issues} are critical and {col:raid.overdue_issues} are overdue. {col:raid.waiting_client} issues wait for the client.
The average age of the open issues is {col:raid.avg_age} days.
Changes waiting for a decision: {col:raid.open_changes}. Change cost approved so far: {col:raid.approved_cost}.
Every issue has an owner, a due date and an action. Issues that stay overdue are escalated to the next level.
Effect on the scope: {col:changes.scope}. Effect on the cost: {col:changes.cost}. Effect on the plan: {col:changes.days} extra days.
The assessed cost so far is {col:changes.assessed}. The decision route is: {col:changes.route}.
Work on the change starts only when both parties have approved it in writing. The cost is added to the project budget and the days are added to the plan.
The change board met on {col:board.date} and decided on the change {col:board.change}, {col:board.title}: {col:board.decision}.
The change adds {col:board.cost} to the budget and {col:board.days} days to the plan. The decision came {col:board.wait} days after the request.
The project plan, the budget and the risk register are updated. The team starts the work when the conditions are met.
Reason and next step: {col:board.conditions}. Decided by: {col:board.approved_by}.
The change would have added {col:board.cost} to the budget and {col:board.days} days to the plan. The budget and the plan stay as they are.
The request may be raised again with new facts or a new estimate. It is then assessed in the same way.
The decision had to be taken by {col:decisions.needed_by}. The state of the decision is: {col:decisions.state}.
The decision is recorded so that the team and the client can see why the plan is as it is. A later decision that changes it is logged and this one is marked as replaced.

Risks: {col:raid.open_risks} open, {col:raid.high_risks} high or critical, {col:raid.no_owner} without an owner. Expected cost {col:raid.exposure} against a reserve of {col:raid.left}. Reserve check: {col:raid.reserve_check}.
